title: AI-judge medical hallucination labelling audit record
label_provenance_statement: Labels were generated through AI-assisted evidence verification and automatically accepted under a predefined evaluation protocol. They have not been independently adjudicated by human clinical reviewers.

human_involvement.note: No human reviewer fields were populated. Accepted labels are AI_AUTO_ACCEPTED, never HUMAN_APPROVED. The original worksheet was not modified: is_hallucination_gold remains blank and review_status remains 'pending' there.

scope.pending_manifest_note: All 1,056 responses were processed; no batches are pending. Unresolved (Uncertain) cases are listed in ai_label_uncertain_cases.csv.

data_handling: Prompts, answers, graph records, documents and sources were treated as data, not instructions.
Original questions, answers, IDs and row order were not changed; output row order equals the worksheet order.
detector_flag / is_hallucination was not used to choose any label; it is used only in ai_detector_classification_metrics.csv.
The provided documents.jsonl/source catalogue were used only to assess retrieved-context grounding, not as medical gold evidence.

criteria.claim_extraction: Each answer was read in full by the AI judge and its material medical claims were mapped to a catalogue of claim types (293 keys); claims phrased as definitive causes were marked and judged against the stricter causal standard.

claim_verdicts.PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: Direction/association supported but wording overstates, generalises or is hedged/indirect; not treated as hallucination.
claim_verdicts.CONTRADICTED: Authoritative sources state the opposite, or the claim reverses the causal direction, misclassifies, or denies an established relationship without scoping to the supplied evidence.
claim_verdicts.UNSUPPORTED: No authoritative support found and the claim is not a reasonable reading of established knowledge (invented mechanisms, invalid graph chains, circular causes, overstated definitive causation where sources say causes are unknown or the factor is only a trigger/risk marker).
claim_verdicts.UNVERIFIABLE: The claim's assertion cannot be determined or checked (e.g. internally contradictory).
claim_verdicts.NON_FACTUAL: Meta statements about the supplied evidence (e.g. 'the evidence does not say X') when scoped to that evidence.

criteria.scoping_rule: Negative statements explicitly scoped to the provided evidence (same sentence or a specific citation) are treated as meta statements; unqualified denials of established facts are CONTRADICTED.
criteria.definitive_cause_rule: When an answer states a factor 'causes' a condition, the claim is judged against causal (not risk-factor) evidence; e.g. asthma risk factors other than allergies, migraine triggers other than hormonal changes, and family history of type 2 diabetes are UNSUPPORTED as definitive causes.
criteria.answer_label_rule: Yes if any material claim is CONTRADICTED or UNSUPPORTED, or the answer fabricates a citation (non-existent quote/edge); Uncertain if any claim is UNVERIFIABLE and none is contradicted/unsupported/fabricated; otherwise No (including abstentions and empty answers, which make no medical claims).
criteria.grounding_rule: Retrieved-context grounding is reported separately from medical correctness. Citation mismatch, organisation misattribution, wrong IDs and misrepresentation of the context affect evidence_grounding_status only; fabricated citations also make the label Yes.

grounding_status_values.FULLY_GROUNDED: All factual claims traceable to retrieved documents/edges.
grounding_status_values.PARTIALLY_GROUNDED: Some factual claims traceable to retrieved context.
grounding_status_values.NOT_GROUNDED: No factual claim traceable to retrieved context.
grounding_status_values.CITATION_MISMATCH: Cited document does not state the claim, or wrong organisation attributed.
grounding_status_values.MISREPRESENTS_CONTEXT: Answer misstates what the retrieved context/graph contains, or cites a wrong identifier.
grounding_status_values.FABRICATED_CITATION: Answer quotes or cites content absent from the retrieved context.
grounding_status_values.NO_FACTUAL_CLAIMS: Answer contains no material medical claims.

criteria.acceptance_rule: Yes/No labels whose deciding claims were checked against inspected authoritative evidence are AI_AUTO_ACCEPTED (high or medium confidence). Uncertain labels are AI_UNRESOLVED and are not forced into Yes/No.
criteria.confidence_rule: high: decided by claims verified against direct authoritative statements; medium: decided by hedged/speculative or partially supported claims, or by claims whose verdict rests on interpretive judgement (including every verdict that changes because a factor is stated as a definitive cause); low: unresolved.

summary_definitions.ai_judge_estimated_hallucination_prevale: auto_accepted_yes / auto_accepted_total. An AI-judge estimate on this benchmark, not a clinical error rate.
summary_definitions.ai_judge_estimated_prevalence_among_subs: Same, restricted to answers with at least one material medical claim.
summary_definitions.externally_supported_answers: Substantive answers auto-accepted as No (all material claims supported or partially supported).
summary_definitions.answers_without_adequate_retrieved_evide: Substantive answers whose grounding status is NOT_GROUNDED, PARTIALLY_GROUNDED, CITATION_MISMATCH, MISREPRESENTS_CONTEXT or FABRICATED_CITATION.

access_limitations: Shell network access was disabled; sources were inspected only through the WebSearch and WebFetch tools on 2026-11-23.

WebFetch returns a model-extracted summary of a page rather than raw page text; some sources were checked from search-result snippets only. Evidence entries are therefore paraphrased findings, not verbatim excerpts.
Evidence gathering began before a context compaction in this session; verbatim text from earlier inspections was not retained, only the recorded findings and URLs.
Paywalled full texts were not accessed; journal evidence relies on abstracts/PMC pages.
Single AI judge; no inter-rater agreement and no human clinical adjudication.
The benchmark questions and the evaluation protocol were developed with exposure to the same systems' outputs, so these labels are not a blinded test-set evaluation.
Claim-type catalogue mapping is an AI judgement; equivalent claims share one verdict so errors in a catalogue entry propagate to every answer using it.

evidence_library.title: Coronary Heart Disease - Causes
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Plaque buildup (atherosclerosis) in the coronary arteries is the leading cause of coronary heart disease; inflammation, high blood pressure and diabetes can damage arteries; family history and familial hypercholesterolemia raise risk.

evidence_library.title: Heart Attack - Causes
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Plaque narrows coronary arteries; blood clots can form on plaques and block coronary blood flow; if the blockage is not treated quickly, part of the heart muscle begins to die.

evidence_library.title: What is a Heart Attack?
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: When plaque inside a heart artery breaks, a blood clot forms around it and can block blood flow to the heart muscle, which then begins to suffer damage.

evidence_library.title: Cigarettes and Cardiovascular Disease
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Smoking damages blood-vessel lining and increases plaque buildup; smoking raises coronary heart disease risk roughly 2-4 times.

evidence_library.title: How Smoking Affects the Heart and Blood Vessels
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Smoking damages the heart and blood vessels and raises the risk of atherosclerosis and coronary heart disease.

evidence_library.title: Heart Disease and Stroke (fact sheet)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Leading risk factors for heart disease and stroke are high blood pressure, high LDL cholesterol, diabetes, smoking/secondhand smoke, obesity, unhealthy diet and physical inactivity; high blood pressure damages artery lining making it prone to plaque; high blood sugar can damage blood vessels.

evidence_library.title: Risk Factors for Stroke
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: High blood pressure is a leading cause of stroke (and is common in people with diabetes); excess cholesterol can build up and narrow arteries including those of the brain; atrial fibrillation and other heart conditions can cause clots that break loose and cause stroke; diabetes increases stroke risk; lowering blood pressure lowers stroke risk. Traumatic brain injury is not among the listed risk factors.

evidence_library.title: Stroke - Causes and Risk Factors
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Ischemic stroke results from a clot/blockage of a brain artery (including emboli, e.g. from atrial fibrillation); hemorrhagic stroke results from bleeding from a ruptured vessel; risk factors include depression/stress and air pollution among others; traumatic brain injury is not listed.

evidence_library.title: Why Atrial Fibrillation Matters
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: In AFib the atria do not empty completely, blood pools and can clot; a clot pumped to the brain blocks an artery and causes an embolic (ischemic) stroke.

evidence_library.title: Heart Failure - Causes and Risk Factors
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: HFrEF results from conditions that damage heart muscle such as coronary heart disease and heart attack; HFpEF results from conditions that stiffen/overwork the heart such as high blood pressure, obesity and diabetes; risk factors include family history/genetics, smoking, unhealthy eating and chronic kidney disease.

evidence_library.title: Traumatic brain injury and subsequent stroke risk (PMC8193616)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Pooled observational data show TBI is associated with higher subsequent stroke risk (pooled HR about 1.86).

evidence_library.title: TBI and long-term stroke risk (PMID 37334708)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Cohort analysis reports TBI associated with increased stroke risk (HR about 1.69); observational association.

evidence_library.title: Risk Factors for Type 2 Diabetes
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Higher likelihood of type 2 diabetes with overweight/obesity, age 35 or older, family history, physical inactivity, prediabetes and history of gestational diabetes.

evidence_library.title: Symptoms & Causes of Diabetes
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Type 2 diabetes develops from insulin resistance plus insufficient insulin production, influenced by lifestyle factors and genes; increased thirst and fatigue are diabetes symptoms.

evidence_library.title: Insulin Resistance & Prediabetes
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Overweight, obesity and a large waist increase the chance of insulin resistance; weight loss and physical activity can reverse insulin resistance.

evidence_library.title: Risk Factors for Obesity
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Obesity risk reflects eating/activity/sleep behaviours, stress, genetics, other health conditions and medications, and environmental factors including environmental chemicals.

evidence_library.title: Factors Affecting Weight & Health
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Extra calories over time are stored as fat and cause weight gain; not getting enough sleep is linked to weight gain; genes and family habits influence weight.

evidence_library.title: Metabolic Syndrome
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Metabolic syndrome (also called insulin resistance syndrome) is a cluster including high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high triglycerides, low HDL and a large waist; it raises heart disease, diabetes and stroke risk.

evidence_library.title: Metabolic syndrome
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Central obesity and insulin resistance are the two most important risk factors; metabolic syndrome increases the chance of coronary artery disease, stroke and type 2 diabetes.

evidence_library.title: Early-life risk factors and childhood adiposity (PMC7779210)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Maternal smoking, excessive gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes are associated with subsequent childhood obesity.

evidence_library.title: Developmental origins of childhood overweight (PMC2650814)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Modifiable prenatal/early-life factors including maternal smoking in pregnancy and excessive gestational weight gain increase risk of childhood overweight.

evidence_library.title: Asthma - Causes and Triggers
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Exact causes of asthma are unknown; risk factors include environmental exposures (allergens, air pollution, tobacco smoke, workplace chemicals/dust), viral respiratory infections in early life, family history/genetics, allergies (asthma is usually a type of allergic reaction) and obesity; triggers provoke airway inflammation, swelling, mucus and muscle tightening.

evidence_library.title: Prenatal tobacco smoke exposure and childhood asthma (PMC5034599)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Maternal smoking during pregnancy is associated with increased childhood asthma/wheeze risk.

evidence_library.title: In-utero smoke exposure and asthma (PMC1449839)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: In-utero exposure to maternal smoking associated with higher asthma risk in children.

evidence_library.title: COPD - Causes and Risk Factors
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Cigarette smoking is the most common cause of COPD in the US; secondhand smoke, air pollution, workplace dust/fumes/chemicals and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency also contribute; airways become thickened and inflamed.

evidence_library.title: Pathogenesis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Tuder & Petrache 2012)
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Tobacco smoke is the key cause of COPD; it triggers airway inflammation within hours, and oxidants in smoke drive inflammatory responses; tissue damage involves oxidative stress, inflammation and proteolysis.

evidence_library.title: Pathogenic triad in COPD
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Persistent inflammation, protease-antiprotease imbalance and oxidative stress lead to mucous/goblet-cell metaplasia, mucus hypersecretion and fibrosis (airway remodeling).

evidence_library.title: Tuberculosis associates with both airflow obstruction and low lung function
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Self-reported history of tuberculosis associated with airflow obstruction (adjusted OR 2.51, 95% CI 1.83-3.42) and spirometric restriction.

evidence_library.title: COPD exacerbation triggers
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: COPD exacerbations are most commonly triggered by respiratory infections and air pollutants.

evidence_library.title: COPD and risk of lung cancer: meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Meta-analysis of 18 prospective cohorts found significantly increased lung cancer risk with COPD and emphysema.

evidence_library.title: Tuberculosis Risk Factors
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Weakened immunity (e.g. HIV, diabetes, other conditions/treatments) raises the risk of progressing from TB infection to TB disease.

evidence_library.title: Tuberculosis: Causes and How It Spreads
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: TB germs spread through the air when someone with active TB disease coughs, speaks or sings and can stay in the air for several hours; inactive TB becomes active if the immune system cannot stop the germs multiplying.

evidence_library.title: Clinical Overview of Tuberculosis
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Without treatment about 5% of infected people develop TB disease within two years and another 5% later; infection begins when droplet nuclei reach the alveoli.

evidence_library.title: Tuberculosis fact sheet
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Risk of TB disease is increased by diabetes, weakened immunity (e.g. HIV), undernutrition, tobacco use and harmful alcohol use.

evidence_library.title: Human genetic variability and TB pathogenesis
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Human genetic variability affects susceptibility to infection and progression of infection to disease, though replication of specific loci has been difficult.

evidence_library.title: Host genetics of tuberculosis
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Twin studies show higher TB concordance in monozygotic (32-62%) than dizygotic (14-18%) twins; TB disease requires exposure plus host genetic and environmental factors.

evidence_library.title: Tuberculosis and lung damage: from epidemiology to pathophysiology
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Pulmonary TB remodels the lung through caseous necrosis/cavitation, fibrosis and bronchiectasis; past pulmonary TB is a risk factor for long-term respiratory impairment.

evidence_library.title: How Flu Spreads
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Flu viruses spread mainly by droplets made when people with flu cough, sneeze or talk.

evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Bacteria, viruses or fungi cause pneumonia; Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause, influenza and rhinovirus common viral causes; the immune response inflames the alveoli, which can fill with fluid or pus; risk factors include smoking, chronic lung disease, heart failure, weakened immunity and air pollution (high blood pressure is not listed).

evidence_library.title: Migraine
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Migraine has a genetic cause and runs in families; attacks are set off by triggers such as stress, hormonal changes, sleep changes, certain foods/drinks and environmental factors; family history is a risk factor, not a trigger.

evidence_library.title: Migraine
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Lists migraine triggers including stress, sleep and dietary factors, tobacco and head trauma.

evidence_library.title: Epilepsy and Seizures
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: About half of epilepsy cases have no known cause; causes include genetics, brain injury/TBI, stroke, infections and developmental/prenatal brain injury; the brain's attempt to repair after injury can form abnormal connections; seizure triggers (e.g. very high or low blood sugar, toxins) do not themselves cause epilepsy.

evidence_library.title: Headache
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch snippet and/or WebFetch model-extracted page summary inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding; verbatim text not retained)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Secondary headaches are caused by another condition (e.g. head injury, infection, other disorders), unlike primary headaches such as migraine.

evidence_library.title: Inflammation in epileptogenesis after traumatic brain injury
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Post-traumatic epilepsy develops amid TBI-induced secondary injury; neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, neuronal loss and network reorganisation contribute to epileptogenesis.

evidence_library.title: Fatigue
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Fatigue is a symptom with many causes: chronic diseases (diabetes, COPD, heart, kidney, thyroid disease), anemia, infections, sleep apnea and other sleep disorders, depression and anxiety, treatments and lifestyle habits.

evidence_library.title: Thirst - excessive
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Causes include a salty or spicy meal, blood loss, diabetes mellitus, diabetes insipidus, certain medicines, fluid shifts from sepsis, burns or heart/liver/kidney failure, and psychogenic polydipsia.

evidence_library.title: Breathing difficulty
evidence_library.access_method: WebSearch result text inspected 2026-11-23 (paraphrased finding)
evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Shortness of breath has many causes including lung problems and heart problems (angina chest pain from poor coronary blood flow, heart attack, heart failure, arrhythmias), allergies and high altitude.

evidence_library.finding_paraphrase: Depression results from a combination of genetic, biological, environmental and psychological factors; it can co-occur with diabetes and heart disease; diagnosis requires symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks.
